Las Vegas property tax is billed by the offices named below.

Who bills what in Las Vegas

  • Clark County Assessor handles assessment.
  • Clark County Treasurer bills and collects the tax.

Due dates

Nevada law (NRS 361.483) installments: 3rd Monday in August, 1st Monday in October, 1st Monday in January, 1st Monday in March (bills over $100 may be paid in installments; 10-day grace period before penalties). Bills mailed once a year; Treasurer page says taxes due 3rd Monday in August.. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Discuss value with the Assessor's appraiser first; appeal to the Clark County Board of Equalization by filing a petition with the Assessor on or before January 15 (next business day if weekend/holiday); forms available from the Assessor in December. Next level is the State Board of Equalization, then District Court.. See the official page.

Tax rate

We could not confirm the current Las Vegas rate on an opened page, so we do not state one.

Local notes

  • Nevada: county assessor values property; county treasurer bills and collects (including for incorporated cities); taxes are by tax district, so rates vary within a city.
  • Las Vegas lies in Clark County; Clark Assessor and Treasurer serve it.
  • Clark Assessor page opened; Board of Equalization page URL taken from search result and not fetched.

Las Vegas by the numbers

With about 650,873 residents, Las Vegas is number 1 of the 14 nv places in this guide by population (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). Census respondents put the median owner-occupied home in Las Vegas at $395,300, 2% below the nv median for these places. Renters live in about 44% of Las Vegas homes, and owners in 56%, where the nv median is 58% owners. A median build year of 1994 puts the typical Las Vegas house near 29 years old. These numbers describe Las Vegas as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.
